title: Fix ledger divergence caused by sequence-length normalization during quantized inference
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers (escalation: ACME-1942, OrionHealth-58) reported small but persistent invoice deltas between Hosted vs Dedicated/Private deployments. Root cause trace points to a sequence-length normalization step in the quantized execution path that applies a per-request rounding heuristic when computing token-equivalent costs. The heuristic differs subtly between hosted aggregator and private runtime which causes 0.1%–0.9% monthly billing skew for heavy short-sequence workloads.
impact_summary: High-revenue customers on Dedicated/Private with short-sequence, high-QPS traffic see month-over-month billing deltas; accounting team receives disputed invoices causing support escalations and manual credits. Affects both hosted and private customers but manifests differently due to an optimization toggle in the quantized kernel selection path.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision a Dedicated cluster with quantized runtime profile (q4_gguf).
Send 2M small (<=16 tokens) streaming requests with bursty QPS and prefix caching enabled.
Compare per-request token accounting emitted by runtime /metrics endpoint vs hosted-aggregator ledger export for same API key/time window.
Observe systematic +rounded token counts in the dedicated export compared to hosted export for the same session IDs.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-02: Initial triage with Support and Billing; obtained CSV exports and matched session_ids (support ticket ACME-1942).
2026-03-03: Found difference in 'seq_norm' multiplier between hosted aggregator and private runtime (diff == 0.012–0.09 per request).
2026-03-04: Hypothesis: quantized path uses int8 token-length bucketing to amortize KV cache costs; hosted path applied a different rounding direction when merging streaming chunks.
2026-03-05: Reproduced locally with instrumented runtime build; added verbose logging to token-accounting module (PR link below).
2026-03-06: Verified that switching the dedicated runtime to 'seq_norm_mode=precise' eliminates delta but increases CPU by ~2% in high-burst tests.
proposed_fix: Unify sequence-length normalization behavior across serving modes by: (1) defaulting to 'precise' normalization for billing-critical tenants, (2) adding a deterministic post-normalization rounding step that preserves idempotency across retries/merges, and (3) exposing a per-tenant toggle to opt into lower-latency bucketed mode if cost-variance accepted.
implementation_todo: Add deterministic rounding helper in /pkg/metering/token_accountant.go (unit tests).
Patch quantized kernel selection to propagate seq_norm_mode flag from control plane to runtime layers.
Add migration: backfill historical exports for disputed ranges when discrepancy > 0.5% (billing team script).
Add e2e test suite: small-sequence streaming harness comparing hosted vs dedicated accounting over 1M requests.
Create feature flag and tenant rollout plan in Console for targeted remediation.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: deploy deterministic rounding helper to runtime-staging clusters and run 48h smoke with heavy short-sequence replay (Mar 11–12). Stage 2: enable seq_norm_mode=precise for impacted tenants via feature-flag (Mar 13). Stage 3: enable default for all Dedicated/Private in runtime-1.23 (Mar 15) with monitoring and optional rollback.
monitoring_and_validation: Add new Grafana panel: per-tenant token-normalization-delta (hosted_export - runtime_export) aggregated hourly.
Add alert: when tenant delta > 0.5% for 6 consecutive hours -> Pager to SRE and BillingOps.
Run post-deploy reconciliation job to compute invoice deltas and auto-generate credit recommendations if needed.
